en.title: Onward, Christian Soldiers
en.author: Sabine Baring-Gould
stanzas:
[D]Onward, Christian soldiers,
[A7]marching as to [D]war,
[D]With the cross of [G]Jesus
[D]going [A7]on be[D]fore!
[D]Christ, the royal [Bm]Master,
[E7]leads against the [A]foe;
[A7]Forward into [D]battle,
[G]see his [A7]banner [D]go!

At the sign of triumph
Satan's host doth flee;
On, then, Christian soldiers,
on to victory!
Hell's foundations quiver
at the shout of praise;
Brothers, lift your voices,
loud your anthems raise!

Crowns and thrones may perish,
Kingdoms rise and wane,
But the Church of Jesus
Constant will remain.
Gates of hell can never
'Gainst that church prevail;
We have Christ's own promise,
And that cannot fail.

Onward, then, ye people,
join our happy throng,
Blend with ours your voices
in the triumph song;
Glory, laud, and honor,
unto Christ the King;
This thro' countless ages
men and angels sing.

notes: Stanzas 1-3 and 5 are hymnary.org's representative text (Baptist Hymnal 1991); stanza 4 ('Crowns and thrones may perish'), commonly printed but absent from that selection, is quoted from the Cyber Hymnal with curly apostrophes normalized to straight. The original's 'What the saints established' stanza is rarely printed and omitted. Cyber Hymnal dates first publication to The Church Times, October 1864; the conventional 1865 date is kept. ST. GERTRUDE (Sullivan) listed in E-flat on hymnary's tune page; moved to D per the guitar rule (D preferred over E on the tie). Chart is the standard simplified changes; the verse's E7-A move to the dominant follows Sullivan.
